## Introduction

In this post, I explore the Palmer Penguins dataset and examine differences in body measurements among penguin species.

## Exploring the Data

First, I load the dataset and inspect the first few rows.

```{python}
import pandas as pd

penguins = pd.read_csv("penguins.csv")

penguins.head()
```
## Average Body Mass by Species

Next, I compare the average body mass of the three penguin species.

```{python}
body_mass_by_species = (
    penguins.groupby("species")["body_mass_g"]
    .mean()
    .sort_values(ascending=False)
)

body_mass_by_species
```
## Summary of Penguin Measurements

Finally, I summarize the body mass and flipper length for each penguin species.

```{python}
penguin_summary = (
    penguins.groupby("species")
    .agg(
        mean_body_mass=("body_mass_g", "mean"),
        mean_flipper_length=("flipper_length_mm", "mean"),
        number_of_penguins=("species", "count")
    )
    .round(2)
)

penguin_summary
```
### Data Source

The Palmer Penguins dataset used in this analysis is from the `palmerpenguins` project by Allison Horst, Alison Hill, and Kristen Gorman. The data were originally collected and made available by Dr. Kristen Gorman and the Palmer Station, Antarctica LTER.

The dataset is available under the CC0 license.
